title: Remapping either Scroll Lock or Num Lock key to Ctrl + [other key] not working

status.label: Needs a current lock-key modifier retest
status.detail: The v0.89.0 report says Num Lock or Scroll Lock mapped to Ctrl+= leaves Ctrl pressed after the first activation; similar older stuck-modifier reports do not establish this sequence is fixed.

next_action.label: Retest Num Lock and Scroll Lock separately
next_action.reason: A current comparison will show whether the old behavior remains after later modifier fixes and whether one lock-key source is responsible.

actions.label: Retest Num Lock and Scroll Lock separately

comment.body: Your v0.89.0 steps say either Num Lock or Scroll Lock mapped to Ctrl+= works once, then leaves Ctrl held until you press it physically. Could you confirm on v0.102.3001 whether this still happens, testing Num Lock and Scroll Lock separately, and whether Ctrl remains down in the On-Screen Keyboard after the first press? If it persists, please add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately after reproducing and say which source key was used. Older #14815 and #17035 reports describe related stuck-modifier symptoms, but neither establishes that this exact lock-key mapping remains unfixed.

judgment.rationale: The original report provides a concrete v0.89.0 sequence and symptom but has no comments or current-version retest. Similar reports #14815 and #17035 describe stuck modifiers, and #17035 links merged PR #37930 for generic modifier side tracking; those do not prove this Num Lock/Scroll Lock source sequence is fixed. Current upstream main's single-key remap path emits an action-key-up followed by modifier key-up on the source key-up event, so the remaining question is whether the event pair is delivered and recognized in this case.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys v0.89.0 from GitHub and remaps Num Lock or Scroll Lock to Ctrl+=.
The first activation works, later activations do nothing, and Ctrl reportedly remains pressed until manually pressed.
There are no comments, current-version test results, or assignees.

Closed #14815 includes a similar Scroll Lock-to-Ctrl+C stuck-modifier report; closed #17035 and merged #37930 concern generic versus left/right modifier tracking, but neither is an exact confirmed fix for this mapping.
Current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 emits the target shortcut action-key-up and modifier key-up on the single-key remap key-up path.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a current-version retest of Num Lock and Scroll Lock separately and a fresh /bugreport only if the stuck state persists.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report may represent a remaining key-event sequencing defect for lock-key sources; the existing main path contains explicit key-up injection, so the current test must establish whether that sequence fails or whether later releases corrected the original behavior.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep synthesized Ctrl state paired for lock-key remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The lock-key source may not produce a matching up/down path that releases the injected Ctrl modifier, or Windows may ignore the generated key-up in this sequence. Current source includes explicit modifier release, so a missing release call is not established.
plan: Reproduce Num Lock-to-Ctrl+= and Scroll Lock-to-Ctrl+= separately on v0.102.3001 and capture a fresh bug report after any stuck state.
Trace source key-down and key-up through the single-key remap handler and verify that Ctrl down, equals down/up, and Ctrl up are all accepted.
If a source-specific event sequence leaves Ctrl logically down, correct the narrow state transition and add tests for both lock-key sources.
Retest repeated activations and verify that the modifier state returns to normal after each one.
verification: Both Num Lock and Scroll Lock can trigger Ctrl+= repeatedly without leaving Ctrl held.
The On-Screen Keyboard and ordinary shortcuts show no residual Ctrl state after the remap.
Existing lock-key toggle behavior remains unchanged when no remap is configured.

confidence.rationale: The original repro is specific, but it predates later modifier changes and current code already emits matching key-up events; a fresh reproduction is needed to localize any remaining defect.
